notes: External native call matching libvorbis vorbis_synthesis_pcmout(vd, &pcm); returns up to `channels` non-interleaved float PCM sample arrays (one FloatArray per channel) currently available from the decoder. Confirmed call site VorbisOggDecoder.kt: `val fs = aDSPState8993!!.pcmOut(aVorbisInfo9006.channels)`, result then consumed and acknowledged via read(fs[0].size).

Private external native constructor helper invoked from the primary constructor's init block (`this.init(arg0); check(!this.b())`); maps to libvorbis vorbis_synthesis_init(vd, vi). Renamed to avoid confusion with Kotlin's init{} block keyword, matching the initInfo/initBlock/initComment pattern used across sibling jagtheora classes. Confirmed constructor call site VorbisOggDecoder.kt: `DSPState(aVorbisInfo9006)`.

External native call matching libvorbis vorbis_synthesis_read(vd, n); tells the decoder that `samples` samples returned by the last pcmOut() call have been consumed, advancing its internal read pointer. Confirmed call site VorbisOggDecoder.kt: `aDSPState8993!!.read(fs!![0]!!.size)`, always called with the exact sample count just retrieved from pcmOut().

External native call matching libvorbis vorbis_synthesis_blockin(vd, vb); feeds a fully-synthesized VorbisBlock (produced by VorbisBlock.synthesis()) into this DSPState for PCM extraction. Confirmed call site VorbisOggDecoder.kt: `if (aVorbisBlock9000!!.synthesis(oggpacket) == 0) aDSPState8993!!.blockIn(aVorbisBlock9000)`, matching the standard libvorbis decode pipeline order (synthesis -> blockin -> pcmout -> read).
External native destructor overriding SimplePeer.clear(); maps to libvorbis vorbis_dsp_clear(vd).

External native call, likely a JNI-side convenience wrapper around libvorbis vorbis_granule_time(vd, granulepos) that uses the decoder's own internally-tracked granule position rather than taking one as an explicit parameter (unlike jagtheora.theora.DecoderContext.granuleTime(GranulePos), which does take an explicit granule position). Confirmed call site VorbisOggDecoder.kt: `aDouble9005 = aDSPState8993!!.granuleTime()`, called with no arguments after blockIn()/pcmOut(), consistent with reporting 'current decode position in seconds'. Confidence medium since the exact native-side computation can't be confirmed without the JNI implementation.
